verses.1: When Israel went forth from Egypt, from the house of Jacob among a people of strangers,
verses.2: Judah became his sanctuary, Israel his dominion.
verses.3: The sea saw and fled, the Jordan turned back.
verses.4: The mountains skipped like rams, the hills like lambs of the flock.
verses.5: What ails you, O sea, that you flee? O Jordan, why do you turn back?
verses.6: O mountains, why do you skip like rams?
verses.7: Before the face of the Lord the earth quaked, before the face of the God of Jacob.
verses.8: You who turned the rock into a pool of water, the flint into a spring of water.

notes:
Notes
- v. 2: "Judah became his sanctuary" reflects the singular use of "קָדְשׁוֹ" as "his sanctuary" rather than a people or object.
- v. 7: "Before the face of the Lord" preserves the Hebrew structure and poetic intensity.
raw:
[1] When Israel went forth from Egypt, from the house of Jacob among a people of strangers,

[2] Judah became his sanctuary, Israel his dominion.

[3] The sea saw and fled, the Jordan turned back.

[4] The mountains skipped like rams, the hills like lambs of the flock.

[5] What ails you, O sea, that you flee? O Jordan, why do you turn back?

[6] O mountains, why do you skip like rams?

[7] Before the face of the Lord the earth quaked, before the face of the God of Jacob.

[8] You who turned the rock into a pool of water, the flint into a spring of water.

---
Notes
- v. 2: "Judah became his sanctuary" reflects the singular use of "קָדְשׁוֹ" as "his sanctuary" rather than a people or object.
- v. 7: "Before the face of the Lord" preserves the Hebrew structure and poetic intensity.
